text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 40

The panel's composition is weak evidence on its own. Economics departments are heavily male, so an all-male panel of four is unremarkable statistically and proves nothing about intent. Lead with it and you look like you're reaching.

Your strong card is the credential gap: completed PhD vs. unfinished, six papers vs. two, four years teaching for a teaching post. That requires explanation regardless of anyone's sex. "Industry experience" may be a legitimate, pre-stated criterion — check the job advert. If it wasn't weighted there, the criteria shifted after the fact.

Chase the written reasons formally; most universities have a deadline. Mention panel composition once, as context. Decide on discrimination after you see their reasoning.
